# Hounsfield Lab

> Hounsfield Lab is a directory of 59 open-source medical AI software tools and 68 public DICOM and NIfTI imaging datasets, curated by a practicing neuroradiologist. Radiology first, plus pathology, clinical NLP and EHR tooling. Tool repository metadata last refreshed 2026-10-19; dataset list last updated 2026-10-26.

Key facts:
- Tool entries record license, commercial-use class, last repository push (UTC) and maintenance status.
- Dataset entries record area, modality, format, size, license, commercial use, access route, whether normals are included, limitations, citation, and the date the source page was last checked.
- Hounsfield Lab links to original sources and does not host code, weights or images.
- Reader-suggested datasets are marked UNVERIFIED until the source page is reviewed.
- Listings are research and development references, not medical, legal or regulatory advice.

Badges: LIC = license (license files reviewed by hand where GitHub could not detect them); UPD = last repository push (UTC); STATUS = Maintained if updated within 12 months of the snapshot, else Stale; COMM = Permissive, Copyleft (GPL/AGPL), Non-commercial, or Verify (custom terms or separate model-weight terms).

## Pages

- [Tool directory](https://hounsfieldlab.com/directory.html): filterable list of all tools
- [DICOM datasets](https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets.html): public imaging datasets with license, access and normals; each has its own page under /datasets/
- [Pipeline guide](https://hounsfieldlab.com/pipeline-orthanc-mercure.html): Orthanc → mercure → TotalSegmentator → OHIF
- [About](https://hounsfieldlab.com/about.html): curation method
- [Full catalog for LLMs](https://hounsfieldlab.com/llms-full.txt)
- [Tool catalog JSON](https://hounsfieldlab.com/data/catalog.json)
- [Dataset JSON](https://hounsfieldlab.com/data/datasets.json)

## Tools: Foundation models & agents

### Pillar-0 (finetune code + HF weights)
- What it is: Open 3D radiology foundation model; finetuning framework, weights on Hugging Face
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: CT (chest, abd-pelvis, head), breast MRI
- Maintainer: YalaLab
- License: ECL-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- License note: Repo LICENSE is Educational Community License 2.0 (Apache 2.0 with a narrowed patent grant). Hugging Face weights (Pillar0-ChestCT, -AbdomenCT, -HeadCT, -BreastMRI) are tagged ecl-2.0.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-12 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/YalaLab/pillar-finetune, https://huggingface.co/collections/YalaLab/pillar-0
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/pillar-0.html
- Related datasets: AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation), C4KC-KiTS, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases, CT Colonography, CT-ORG, Duke-Breast-Cancer-MRI

### Pillar-0 pretraining
- What it is: Vision-language pretraining code for Pillar-0
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Radiology CT/MRI
- Maintainer: YalaLab
- License: ECL-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- License note: Repo LICENSE is Educational Community License 2.0.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-01-13 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/YalaLab/pillar-pretrain
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/pillar-0-pretraining.html

### RATE
- What it is: Uses an LLM (Qwen3 via sglang) to extract structured labels for 366 findings from radiology reports
- Type: Evaluation / report labeling
- Modality/specialty: Radiology reports
- Maintainer: YalaLab
- License: ECL-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- License note: Repo LICENSE is Educational Community License 2.0.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-05-20 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/YalaLab/rate
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/rate.html

### Merlin
- What it is: 3D vision-language model for CT that uses structured EHR and report supervision
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: CT
- Maintainer: Stanford MIMI
- License: MIT
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-09-24 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/StanfordMIMI/Merlin
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/merlin.html
- Related datasets: AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation), C4KC-KiTS, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases, CT Colonography, CT-ORG, Pancreas-CT

### MedGemma
- What it is: Google's open medical model family; repo has notebooks and code
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Multimodal medical (imaging + text)
- Maintainer: Google Health
- License: Apache-2.0 (code)
- Commercial use: Verify
- License note: Code is Apache-2.0. Weights on Hugging Face are under the Health AI Developer Foundations terms: https://developers.google.com/health-ai-developer-foundations/terms

- Last repository update: 2026-06-19 (Maintained)

- Modality/specialty: Radiology: chest X-ray

- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive

### LLaVA-Med
- What it is: Biomedical vision-language assistant for image Q&A
- Type: Vision-language model
- Modality/specialty: Biomedical multimodal
- Maintainer: Microsoft
- License: Microsoft Research License
- Commercial use: Verify
- License note: Repo LICENSE is the Microsoft Research License Terms, covering code, models and data. Read the terms before any use beyond research.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2025-06-04 (Stale)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/microsoft/LLaVA-Med
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/llava-med.html

### RadFinder
- What it is: 3D CT vision-language model for report-to-scan retrieval, prompt-based disease classification and slice-level localization; RadFinder-2610 checkpoints released Oct 22, 2026
- Type: Vision-language model
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: 3D CT (chest, abdomen-pelvis)
- Maintainer: University of Freiburg (LMB) / Ging et al.
- License: MIT (code); CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (weights)
- Commercial use: Non-commercial
- License note: Code is MIT, except files in src/rate/ vendored from YalaLab/rate, which are ECL-2.0. Hugging Face weights (lmb-freiburg/radfinder-2610-full, -refct, -public, -ctrate) are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and also subject to the training datasets' licenses (e.g. CT-RATE is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Published at MICCAI 2026.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-22 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/lmb-freiburg/radfinder, https://huggingface.co/collections/lmb-freiburg/radfinder
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/radfinder.html

### MedVTok
- What it is: General-purpose medical visual tokenizer that encodes 2D images and 3D volumes into one token space (global features, patch tokens and latents) for classification, retrieval, segmentation, synthesis, VQA and report generation; trained on over 28M images and 70K volumes
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Multimodal: 2D images and 3D CT/MRI volumes (9 modalities incl. X-ray, ultrasound, pathology)
- Maintainer: Ma, Ji, Ning, Liu et al. (Masaaki-75)
- License: MIT
- Commercial use: Permissive
- License note: Repo LICENSE and the Hugging Face model card (massaki75/medvtok, public, not gated, checkpoint downloaded with hf download) state MIT. Training uses features from several expert encoders and public datasets that carry their own terms. Paper: arXiv 2610.35842 (Oct 26, 2026).
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-27 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/Masaaki-75/medvtok, https://huggingface.co/massaki75/medvtok
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/medvtok.html

### RadKev
- What it is: Open-weight radiology decision models (9B and 27B adapters) that score fixed-choice radiology questions in one forward pass without generating text
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Radiology (report and case decision tasks)
- Maintainer: U. Wisconsin–Madison (Ram / Zhang)
- License: Apache-2.0 (code); CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (weights)
- Commercial use: Non-commercial
- License note: Code is Apache-2.0. Hugging Face adapters (ramu9703/radkev-27b, radkev-9b) are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial research; gated access requires accepting those terms. Not a medical device.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-07 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/udiram/RadKev, https://huggingface.co/ramu9703/radkev-27b
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/radkev.html

## Tools: Segmentation & frameworks

### MONAI
- What it is: PyTorch-based AI toolkit for healthcare imaging
- Type: Framework
- Modality/specialty: Medical imaging (all)
- Maintainer: Project MONAI (NVIDIA + academic)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-19 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAI
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/monai.html
- Related datasets: B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver, Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy, ReMIND (preoperative MRI and intraoperative ultrasound), Sunnybrook Cardiac Data, COCA, EchoNet-Dynamic

### MONAI Label
- What it is: AI-assisted image labeling and active learning; integrates with 3D Slicer and OHIF
- Type: Annotation
- Modality/specialty: Medical imaging
- Maintainer: Project MONAI
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-19 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAILabel
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/monai-label.html
- Related datasets: B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver, Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy, ReMIND (preoperative MRI and intraoperative ultrasound), EchoNet-Dynamic, Open POCUS, Thyroid Ultrasound Cine-clip

### nnU-Net
- What it is: Self-configuring segmentation framework
- Type: Segmentation
- Modality/specialty: Medical imaging (all)
- Maintainer: DKFZ (MIC)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-16 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/nnu-net.html
- Related datasets: AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation), Breast-Cancer-Screening-DBT (BCS-DBT), C4KC-KiTS, CBIS-DDSM, CMMD, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases

### TotalSegmentator
- What it is: Segments more than 100 anatomical structures in CT and MR
- Type: Segmentation
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: CT/MR
- Maintainer: J. Wasserthal
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-16 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/wasserth/TotalSegmentator
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/totalsegmentator.html
- Related datasets: AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation), C4KC-KiTS, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases, CT Colonography, CT-ORG, FDG-PET-CT-Lesions (autoPET)

### NV-Segment-CT
- What it is: CT segmentation built from MONAI VISTA3D: 117 structures automatically, or 132 promptable by point or class. Research use only, not for clinical care. Needs a CUDA GPU; weights are about 872 MB
- Type: Segmentation
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: CT
- Maintainer: NVIDIA
- License: Apache-2.0 (code); NVIDIA Open Model License (weights)
- Commercial use: Verify
- License note: Hugging Face LICENSE applies Apache-2.0 to every file except the weights. Weights (model.pt is 872 MB) are under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which says the models are commercially usable; it is a custom license, not an OSI license (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/agreements/enterprise-software/nvidia-open-model-license/, last modified October 24, 2025). The model card limits use to research and says it is not for clinical use. Inference expects a CUDA GPU (Ampere or Hopper). NV-Segment-CTMR is a different, non-commercial model and is not this listing.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-05 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NV-Segment-CT, https://github.com/NVIDIA-Medtech/NV-Segment-CTMR
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/nv-segment-ct.html
- Related datasets: AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation), C4KC-KiTS, Colorectal-Liver-Metastases, CT Colonography, CT-ORG, FDG-PET-CT-Lesions (autoPET)

### SlimFormer++
- What it is: Lightweight (5.98M-parameter) 3D segmentation network packaged as an nnU-Net v2 trainer, with pretrained weights for ACDC (cardiac MRI), AbdomenCT-1K and AMOS2022 CT and a 3D Slicer extension for 15 abdominal organs in CT
- Type: Segmentation
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: 3D CT, MRI, ultrasound
- Maintainer: Hong, Zhang, Liu, Mo, Ye (University of Exeter)
- License: SlimFormer++ Noncommercial Research License 1.0
- Commercial use: Non-commercial
- License note: Repo LICENSE permits noncommercial scientific research only; commercial use, including products and paid consulting, needs separate written permission. Third-party parts stay Apache-2.0. The Slicer extension code (WHHHHHY822/SlicerSlimFormerPlusPlus) is Apache-2.0 but its model weights follow the noncommercial license. Requires Linux, an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA 12.6 to build. Paper: arXiv 2610.25488.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-24 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus, https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlicerSlimFormerPlusPlus, https://huggingface.co/Yang0822/SlimFormerPlusPlus-AMOS2022-CT
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/slimformer-plus-plus.html

- Modality/specialty: Medical imaging (2D)

### ContiLNN
- What it is: Adds bidirectional liquid-neural modules along the slice axis to 2D restoration backbones; pretrained checkpoints for CT denoising, MRI super-resolution and low-count PET
- Type: Data / preprocessing
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: CT; MRI; PET
- Maintainer: ContiLNN authors (Kunming UST / collaborators)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Permissive
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-09 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/Noah-hjl/ContiLNN
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/contilnn.html

### TorchXRayVision
- What it is: Library of chest X-ray dataset loaders and pretrained classification, segmentation and autoencoder models
- Type: Framework
- Modality/specialty: Radiology: chest X-ray
- Maintainer: mlmed
- License: Apache-2.0 (library); models vary
- Commercial use: Verify
- License note: LICENSE says the main library is Apache-2.0 and that licenses vary by subpackage; check each baseline model's license before use.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-18 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/mlmed/torchxrayvision
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/torchxrayvision.html
- Related datasets: LIDC-IDRI, MIDRC-RICORD (1A, 1B, 1C), NCI Imaging Data Commons, NIH ChestX-ray14, CheXpert Plus, RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge

### Brain2Vec
- What it is: Self-supervised 3D masked-autoencoder foundation model pretrained on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRIs; used as a fine-tuning backbone or frozen feature extractor (e.g., brain age, disease classification)
- Type: Foundation model
- Modality/specialty: Neuro: structural T1-weighted brain MRI
- Maintainer: UPenn CBICA (Davatzikos lab)
- License: CBICA non-commercial agreement (code); CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (weights)
- Commercial use: Non-commercial
- License note: The repo LICENSE points to the UPenn CBICA non-commercial software agreement (https://www.med.upenn.edu/cbica/software-agreement-non-commercial.html). Weights on Hugging Face (cbica/Brain2Vec) are gated with manual approval and tagged CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Inputs must be skull-stripped and linearly registered to the provided template; the repo added a preprocessing pipeline for this on Oct 27, 2026 (NiChart_DLMUSE skull-stripping, then FSL flirt). Paper: arXiv 2610.28411 (Oct 20, 2026).
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-27 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec, https://huggingface.co/cbica/Brain2Vec
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/brain2vec.html

### FastSurfer
- What it is: Deep-learning whole-brain segmentation and cortical surface reconstruction, a fast alternative to FreeSurfer recon-all
- Type: Neuroimaging suite
- Modality/specialty: Neuroradiology: brain MRI
- Maintainer: Deep-MI (DZNE)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Commercial use: Verify
- License note: Repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0. The surface pipeline calls FreeSurfer binaries and needs a FreeSurfer license file (free, separate terms). The README says results are for research and not for clinical decision support.
- Access: free public source repository
- Last repository update: 2026-10-18 (Maintained)
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Links: https://github.com/Deep-MI/FastSurfer
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/tools/fastsurfer.html
- Related datasets: CFB-GBM, ISLES'24, IXI, Medical Segmentation Decathlon, NCI Imaging Data Commons, OpenNeuro

## DICOM datasets

### AMOS (abdominal multi-organ segmentation)
- What it is: Multi-center abdominal CT and MRI from patients with a range of diseases, with voxel labels for 15 abdominal organs
- Source: https://zenodo.org/records/7262581
- Area: body
- Modality: CT; MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 500 CT and 100 MRI scans (240 train, 120 validation, 240 test); one 24.2 GB zip
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7262581) and download amos22.zip and the metadata CSV. No account is needed. The record links separate Zenodo records for the unlabeled CT and MRI scans.
- Limitations: Labels are organ anatomy (spleen, kidneys, gallbladder, esophagus, liver, stomach, aorta, IVC, pancreas, adrenals, duodenum, bladder, prostate/uterus), not disease, and scans are not labeled normal or abnormal. NIfTI in the nnU-Net folder layout, not DICOM. Built for the MICCAI 2022 AMOS challenge; confirm which splits carry labels before you benchmark. Organ sizes are long-tailed, so small structures such as the adrenals are hard.
- Citation: Yes. Cite Ji et al., AMOS: A Large-Scale Abdominal Multi-Organ Benchmark for Versatile Medical Image Segmentation, NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv:2206.08023), and the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7262581. CC BY 4.0 requires attribution.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-26
- Last checked: 2026-10-26
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/amos-abdominal-multi-organ-segmentation.html

### B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver
- What it is: Focal liver lesions on B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/b-mode-and-ceus-liver/
- Area: ultrasound
- Modality: US
- Normals included: no
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 120 subjects
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
- Limitations: Liver-lesion cohort (the TCIA diagnosis list is liver cancer). It is not a normal-liver screening set. CEUS clips and B-mode stills are different series. Confirm which diagnoses are malignant versus benign in the clinical table.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/b-mode-and-ceus-liver.html

### BrainMetShare
- What it is: Brain metastases with radiologist segmentations on a subset
- Source: https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/1emj-bjxt3p6s0
- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: no
- Format: Check source
- Size: 156 MRI studies; about 5.6 GB. Masks for 105 studies.
- License: Stanford AIMI research use agreement (non-commercial; commercial license sold separately)
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: account
- How to access: Sign in on Redivis, open this dataset, and apply for access. Accept the Stanford research-use terms for this dataset (each dataset is a separate request). Non-commercial research is free. Commercial use needs a separate AIMI license: https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets-commercial-use
- Limitations: Free access is for non-commercial research under a data-use agreement. Do not redistribute the files or the download link. Do not attempt to re-identify anyone. A paid commercial license is a different contract; check the current fee and terms on the AIMI commercial-use page. Every case has at least one metastasis. Images are skull-stripped and co-registered, not raw DICOM. Confirm the container format (often processed volumes rather than DICOM) on download. 51 cases are held out without public masks.
- Citation: Yes. DOI 10.71718/z66c-qr59, as printed on the AIMI BrainMetShare page.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/brainmetshare.html

### Breast-Cancer-Screening-DBT (BCS-DBT)

### Burdenko-GBM-Progression
- What it is: Glioblastoma radiotherapy planning and follow-up, with RTSTRUCT/RTDOSE/RTPLAN
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/burdenko-gbm-progression/
- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR; CT
- Normals included: no
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 180 subjects; about 131 GB of imaging
- License: NIH Controlled Data Access Policy (images); CC BY 4.0 (clinical and genomic CSV)
- Commercial use allowed: check
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: The images can reconstruct a face, so they are not an open download. Follow the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy link on the collection page. The clinical and genomic CSV is listed separately under CC BY 4.0.
- Limitations: Do not assume the whole collection is CC BY. Only the small clinical/genomic table is CC BY 4.0. Imaging requires controlled access. Some MRIs are not in a canonical orientation. Registration between MRI and planning CT is not included; the submitters point to an external alignment container.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy. Imaging access is governed by the NIH policy, not only by CC BY.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/burdenko-gbm-progression.html

### CFB-GBM
- What it is: Glioblastoma, with pre- and post-treatment MRI, planning CT, RTDOSE, tumor masks, and GTV
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/cfb-gbm/
- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR; CT
- Normals included: no
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 264 subjects; about 208 GB (3,981 images in the NIfTI package)
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. Images and segmentations are one NIfTI package, and that row requires the IBM Aspera Connect plugin. Clinical, treatment, imaging-availability, RANO, and PyRadiomics TSVs are separate small downloads on the same table.
- Limitations: NIfTI only, and skull-stripped. DICOM is deliberately not provided, to avoid leakage of header metadata. MRI brain extraction used ANTsPyNet on the pre-treatment post-contrast T1, and the other MRI series were rigidly registered to that scan. Planning CT was defaced with TotalSegmentator (thermoplastic mask removal) and then CTA-DEFACE. Not healthy controls: 264 deceased adults with glioblastoma, treated with the Stupp protocol at one center (Centre François Baclesse) from November 2017 to December 2023, and not enrolled in a trial. Not every sequence or time point exists for every patient (planning CT 195, RTDOSE 194; tumor masks follow the post-contrast T1 exams). GTV contours are from routine radiotherapy planning. Clinical, treatment, and RANO TSVs are included, plus a PyRadiomics feature table. Version 4 (updated 2026-09-11) corrected the RANO TSV to enhancing-tumor measurements and renumbered some folders; the images were not changed.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page (10.7937/v9pn-2f72, version 4) and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-21
- Last checked: 2026-10-21
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/cfb-gbm.html

### CheXpert Plus
- What it is: Chest radiographs with full reports and 14 CheXpert pathology labels, including studies without those findings
- Source: https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/5yyj-1a9f6ap0x
- Area: chest
- Modality: DX; CR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 223,462 radiograph–report pairs; 187,711 studies; 64,725 patients; about 6.8 TB
- License: Stanford AIMI research use agreement (non-commercial; commercial license sold separately)
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: account
- How to access: Sign in on Redivis, open this dataset, and apply for access. Accept the Stanford research-use terms for this dataset (each dataset is a separate request). Non-commercial research is free. Commercial use needs a separate AIMI license: https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets-commercial-use
- Limitations: Free access is for non-commercial research under a data-use agreement. Do not redistribute the files or the download link. Do not attempt to re-identify anyone. A paid commercial license is a different contract; check the current fee and terms on the AIMI commercial-use page. DICOM plus the report text, split into sections. Labels include an uncertain class. This is the plus release (reports and DICOM), not the original CheXpert JPEG label release. A hospital mix, not healthy volunteers.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the dataset DOI or the citation block on the Redivis page, and name Stanford AIMI.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18

### CT-ICH
- What it is: Traumatic brain injury head CT with hemorrhage masks and slice labels; some scans have no hemorrhage
- Source: https://physionet.org/content/ct-ich/
- Area: neuro
- Modality: CT
- Normals included: partial
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 75 public NIfTI subjects (82 collected; subjects 59–65 are missing from the image folder)
- License: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data License 1.5.0
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: Create a PhysioNet account and sign the Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0 on the project (current version 1.3.1). Research use only. An older 1.2.0 release was CC BY 4.0; do not assume that still applies.

### Healthy-Total-Body-CTs
- What it is: Healthy adult total-body low-dose CT from the uEXPLORER PET/CT scanner, with organ segmentations
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/healthy-total-body-cts/
- Area: body
- Modality: CT
- Normals included: yes
- Format: DICOM; NIfTI
- Size: 30 subjects; 30 studies; CT images about 59 GB (58.95 GB in the download table). Segmentations about 109 MB
- License: NIH Controlled Data Access Policy (CT images); CC BY 4.0 (organ segmentations and demographics)
- Commercial use allowed: check
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: The CT images can reconstruct a face, so they are not an open download. Follow the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy link on the collection page. Request the images in dbGaP (the policy page lists phs004225, Radiology Imaging Data Containing Faces from The Cancer Imaging Archive, for most TCIA face datasets). The request has to come from someone equivalent to a tenure-track professor or a senior scientist. After approval, create an NCI Data Commons API key and download with the TCIA Data Retriever using the manifest in the Data Access table. Organ segmentations (NIfTI and an organ-values spreadsheet) and the demographics spreadsheet are listed separately under CC BY 4.0 and do not need an application.
- Limitations: Do not assume the whole collection is CC BY. Only the segmentations and demographics are CC BY 4.0. The CT requires controlled access. Thirty healthy adults, not a cancer cohort, scanned on the UC Davis uEXPLORER total-body PET/CT system; only the CT is distributed here. The 90-minute CT was about 50 mAs and the other time points about 5 mAs, all at 140 kVp. Each person has three or six same-day time points, stored as one study in version 3. Segmentations cover 37 tissues, were made with MOOSE on the 90-minute scan, and are NIfTI that may need re-orientation to match the DICOM. Version 3 (updated 2026-09-23) corrected NIfTI file names to match the DICOM.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page (10.7937/nc7z-4f76, version 3) and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy. Imaging access is governed by the NIH policy, not only by CC BY.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-21
- Last checked: 2026-10-21
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/healthy-total-body-cts.html

### Medical Segmentation Decathlon
- What it is: Ten segmentation tasks: brain tumor, hippocampus, lung tumor, liver tumor, pancreas tumor, colon cancer, hepatic vessels, spleen, prostate, and left atrium
- Source: https://registry.opendata.aws/msd/
- Area: neuro; chest; body; cardiac
- Modality: CT; MR
- Normals included: no
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: Ten tasks, from 30 to 750 volumes each; test labels are not released
- License: CC BY-SA 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Use the AWS Open Data page. The bucket s3://msd-for-monai can be listed and downloaded with the AWS CLI and --no-sign-request, so no AWS account is needed. MONAI also ships a loader for these tasks. Task descriptions are on medicaldecathlon.com.
- Limitations: Built for a 2018 segmentation challenge, so each task targets one structure or lesion and the cohorts are small for some tasks (left atrium has 30 volumes). Test-set labels are withheld. The brain tumor task is drawn from BraTS 2016–2017 and the lung task from TCIA, so check overlap before combining with those sources. Share-alike applies if you redistribute adapted data.
- Citation: Yes. Cite Simpson et al., A large annotated medical image dataset for the development and evaluation of segmentation algorithms (arXiv:1902.09063), and Antonelli et al., Nature Communications 2022.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-19
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/medical-segmentation-decathlon.html

### MIDRC
- What it is: Medical imaging, especially chest and COVID-era collections, with clinical data and reports where contributors included them
- Source: https://data.midrc.org/
- Area: chest
- Modality: CT; DX; CR; MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM
- Size: Portal; size depends on the collections you select
- License: University of Chicago data-use agreement (non-commercial research by default; a separate commercial agreement exists)
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: Register at data.midrc.org (InCommon or ORCID, as the login page offers) and accept the data-use agreement. The current text is linked from https://www.midrc.org/midrc-data-use-agreement and from the portal. Download only after the agreement is accepted.
- Limitations: The default academic agreement is personal, non-commercial research at a non-profit or government institution. It forbids redistributing the data, and it is not a Creative Commons license. A commercial agreement is a different document. Collections can include reports and clinical fields; do not treat every row as images alone. RICORD on TCIA is CC BY-NC and is not this portal.
- Citation: Yes. Acknowledge MIDRC in presentations and papers, using the wording on https://www.midrc.org/midrc-acknowledgements
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/midrc.html

Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. - Limitations: Non-commercial only. 1A is COVID-19 chest CT. 1B adds CT controls. 1C is chest radiographs with COVID and non-COVID labels. These TCIA collections are the RICORD challenge sets, not the whole MIDRC portal. Pixel labels are not full reports.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/midrc-ricord-1a-1b-1c.html

### MIMIC-CXR
- What it is: Emergency and inpatient chest radiographs with free-text reports, across many findings and no-finding studies
- Source: https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/
- Area: chest
- Modality: DX; CR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 377,110 images; 227,835 studies (version 2.1.0)
- License: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: Create a PhysioNet account, complete CITI “Data or Specimens Only Research” training, and sign the Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. Download the DICOM release (version 2.1.0), not only MIMIC-CXR-JPG, if you need DICOM.
- Limitations: Credentialed research use only. No sharing, no re-identification, and code from papers that use the data should be shared back. Reports are included and were de-identified (PHI replaced with ___). Images had burned-in text removed. This is a hospital population, so “normal” means no acute finding was described, not a healthy-volunteer study. JPEG derivatives are a different PhysioNet project.
- Citation: Yes. Johnson et al., MIMIC-CXR Database (version 2.1.0), PhysioNet. https://doi.org/10.13026/4jqj-jw95
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/mimic-cxr.html

### MRNet
- What it is: Knee MRI exams labeled for abnormality, ACL tear, and meniscal tear
- Source: https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/4a2c-4cpkzrn2c
- Area: msk
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: NumPy
- Size: 1,370 exams; about 7.7 GB on the AIMI listing
- License: Stanford AIMI research use agreement (non-commercial; commercial license sold separately)
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: account
- How to access: Sign in on Redivis, open this dataset, and apply for access. Accept the Stanford research-use terms for this dataset (each dataset is a separate request). Non-commercial research is free. Commercial use needs a separate AIMI license: https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets-commercial-use
- Limitations: Free access is for non-commercial research under a data-use agreement. Do not redistribute the files or the download link. Do not attempt to re-identify anyone. A paid commercial license is a different contract; check the current fee and terms on the AIMI commercial-use page. The public release is exam volumes as arrays, not a DICOM PACS export. About 19% of exams were read as normal. Labels were taken from reports; the reports themselves are not the dataset.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the dataset DOI or the citation block on the Redivis page, and name Stanford AIMI.

- Added: 2026-10-18

### NCI Imaging Data Commons
- What it is: Many cancer collections (TCGA, TCIA, CPTAC, NLST, LIDC, and others), harmonized to DICOM
- Source: https://portal.imaging.datacommons.cancer.gov/collections/
- Area: neuro; chest; body; breast; nuclear medicine
- Modality: CT; MR; PT; MG; CR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM
- Size: Portal of public cancer imaging, described by NCI as over 100 TB
- License: Mostly CC BY; a minority of files are CC-NC (each file is tagged)
- Commercial use allowed: check
- Access: open
- How to access: Browse collections in the portal. No registration. Files are in Google and AWS public buckets. Filter or inspect the license tag on each file before a commercial project.
- Limitations: This is a portal, not one cohort. More than 95% of files are described as CC BY, which allows commercial reuse with attribution, but a subset is CC-NC. De-identification and face-reconstruction risk still apply to head imaging. Not a substitute for reading the license on the files you actually download.
- Citation: Yes. Cite IDC and the underlying collection.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/nci-imaging-data-commons.html

### NIH ChestX-ray14
- What it is: Frontal chest radiographs with 14 text-mined thoracic finding labels (such as effusion, nodule, pneumothorax) plus No Finding
- Source: https://nihcc.app.box.com/v/ChestXray-NIHCC
- Area: chest
- Modality: DX
- Normals included: yes
- Format: PNG
- Size: 112,120 images from 30,805 patients
- License: NIH Clinical Center terms (no use restrictions; attribution required)
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the NIH Clinical Center Box folder and download the image archives, the label CSV, and the bounding-box CSV. No account is needed. Google Cloud also hosts a copy as a public dataset.
- Limitations: Labels were text-mined from reports by NLP and are estimated to be more than 90% accurate, so expect label noise. The reports themselves are not released. Only a small subset has bounding boxes. Images are PNG, not DICOM. Single institution. Many images are follow-up studies of the same patients, so split by patient ID.
- Citation: Yes. The terms ask you to link the NIH download site, cite Wang et al., ChestX-ray8, IEEE CVPR 2017, and acknowledge the NIH Clinical Center as the data provider.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-26
- Last checked: 2026-10-26
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/nih-chestx-ray14.html

A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The full NLST clinical dataset is still requested through the Cancer Data Access System (CDAS). TCIA hosts the CT images and a public subset of the clinical data.
- Limitations: The TCIA copy is the public imaging release and a limited clinical subset, not every NLST variable. Screening CTs are low-dose and include a large majority of examinations without cancer. Histopathology slides are a separate download. Cite NLST as well as TCIA.

### NYU fastMRI
- What it is: Raw k-space and reconstructed MRI from clinical knee, brain, prostate, and breast exams, built for accelerated MRI reconstruction research
- Source: https://fastmri.med.nyu.edu/
- Area: msk; neuro; body; breast
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM; HDF5
- Size: Over 1,500 raw knee and 10,000 DICOM knee exams, 6,970 raw brain exams, 312 prostate and 300 breast exams
- License: NYU fastMRI Dataset Sharing Agreement (internal research or education only)
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: account
- How to access: Read the Dataset Sharing Agreement on the fastMRI page and submit the online application with your institutional affiliation and intended use. Approved users get a personal download link. Each sub-dataset has its own agreement.
- Limitations: Internal research or education only. No redistribution, no sharing of the download link, no selling or monetizing, and no attempt to re-identify anyone; the agreement also asks you to destroy copies when your work is done. Most data are raw k-space for reconstruction, not diagnostic labels. DICOM is described for the knee set only. Not for clinical use.
- Citation: Yes. The agreement requires citing “NYU fastMRI” and Knoll et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2020 (doi 10.1148/ryai.2020190007), plus arXiv:1811.08839.
- Status: VERIFIED

- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: Repository of public BIDS datasets (size is per dataset)
- License: Per dataset, usually CC0 after a 36-month grace period (check source)
- Commercial use allowed: check
- Access: open
- How to access: Search OpenNeuro and open a dataset. Public versions download without a data-use agreement. Read that dataset’s license, README, and version DOI. New uploads can sit in a grace period before they are public.
- Limitations: Almost all current releases are CC0, but the license is per dataset and older uploads varied. These are BIDS NIfTI, not clinical DICOM. Many datasets are small research cohorts. Facial features on structural MRI are supposed to be removed; still do not try to re-identify subjects.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the version DOI. A HowToAcknowledge field, when present, is the authors’ requested wording. CC0 itself does not legally require attribution.

### Sunnybrook Cardiac Data
- What it is: Cine cardiac MRI: healthy, hypertrophy, heart failure with infarction, and heart failure without infarction
- Source: https://sourceforge.net/projects/cardiac-mr/files/
- Area: cardiac
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: partial
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 45 cases in 3 DICOM parts plus contours; SourceForge lists about 608 MB for the project files
- License: CC0 1.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Download the original 2009 challenge release from the SourceForge project page: three DICOM zip parts, three contour zip parts, and the age and gender table. The README states CC0 1.0 Universal (changed from Open Data Commons PDDL on 2 Sept 2010). No account is required. The Cardiac Atlas page that used to host a five-batch copy of this set no longer resolves.
- Limitations: Small challenge set. Pathologies are mixed with healthy cases. Contours are the left ventricle from the 2009 short-axis segmentation challenge, in the challenge’s three parts (online contest, validation, and training). This is that SourceForge release, not the later Cardiac Atlas packaging of five DICOM batches and a CAP ID crosswalk CSV, which is no longer online. CC0 does not require attribution. The former project page asked you to cite Radau et al. if you publish; the SourceForge README does not.
- Citation: Requested, not required by CC0. Radau et al., Evaluation Framework for Algorithms Segmenting Short Axis Cardiac MRI. The MIDAS Journal. http://hdl.handle.net/10380/3070
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-21
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/sunnybrook-cardiac-data.html

### TotalSegmentator CT dataset
- What it is: Routine clinical CT scans with segmentations of 117 anatomical structures (organs, bones, muscles, vessels); version 3 adds 291 pediatric CTs
- Source: https://zenodo.org/records/22688904
- Area: body; chest; msk
- Modality: CT
- Normals included: partial
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 1,939 CT images (version 3.0.0); one 37.4 GB zip
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the Zenodo record and download the zip. No account is needed. The record also links a faster Dropbox copy and a 102-subject subset for a quick look. Earlier versions (1,228 images) remain on Zenodo under their own DOIs.
- Limitations: Labels are anatomy, not disease, and the scans have no normal or abnormal label even though many pathologies are present. NIfTI, not DICOM. The segmentations were made with a model-assisted workflow, so they can carry systematic errors; version 3 fixed many label errors and vertebra mix-ups. The paper describes version 1.
- Citation: Yes. The record asks you to cite Wasserthal et al., TotalSegmentator, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023, and the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22688904.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-19
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/totalsegmentator-ct-dataset.html

### UCSD-BMETS-Longitudinal
- What it is: Brain metastases, longitudinal pre- and post-treatment MRI with neuroradiologist-approved segmentations
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/ucsd-bmets-longitudinal/
- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: no
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 300 subjects; 1,066 studies; about 163 GB
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The MRI and segmentation package is NIfTI, not DICOM, and that row requires the IBM Aspera Connect plugin. The clinical TSV, data dictionaries, and MRI metadata TSV are separate small downloads on the same table.
- Limitations: Not DICOM. DICOM was converted with dcm2niix and skull-stripped with HD-BET, then registered to the contrast T1 from the first time point. Segmentations are NIfTI masks in that same space (BraTS compartments: enhancing tissue, non-enhancing tumor core, FLAIR hyperintensity, and resection cavity), approved by a neuroradiologist after nnU-Net pre-segmentation. Not healthy controls. Two to four time points per patient, before and after treatment; a pre-diagnosis MRI was included for some patients with fewer than four scans. Every exam has pre-contrast T1, post-contrast T1, T2, and FLAIR; other sequences are missing on some exams. The download table lists 1,066 studies and 11,405 images. The collection text says 1,065 MRI time points. Clinical data are in a TSV. Updated 2026-10-05.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page (10.7937/5ejb-9g94) and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-21
- Last checked: 2026-10-21
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/ucsd-bmets-longitudinal.html

### UCSF-PDGM
- What it is: Preoperative diffuse glioma (WHO grade 2–4) on a standardized 3T protocol, with IDH and MGMT status, BraTS-style tumor segmentations, and diffusion and ASL perfusion
- Source: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/ucsf-pdgm/
- Area: neuro
- Modality: MR
- Normals included: no
- Format: NIfTI
- Size: 495 patients (501 exams); about 142 GB
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Commercial use allowed: yes
- Access: open
- How to access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The image download uses IBM Aspera Connect.
- Limitations: Glioma cohort, not healthy controls. TCIA states the original DICOM is not available: images are skull-stripped, co-registered to the FLAIR at 1 mm, and released as NIfTI. Six IDs turned out to be follow-up scans of other patients and were renamed in version 3. A metadata sheet maps cases to BraTS 2021 IDs, so check for overlap before combining with BraTS. Single center, single scanner vendor.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI 10.7937/tcia.bdgf-8v37 and Calabrese et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2022, and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-19
- Last checked: 2026-10-19
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/ucsf-pdgm.html

### VinDr-CXR
- What it is: Adult chest radiographs with radiologist bounding boxes and image-level diagnoses, including no-finding exams
- Source: https://physionet.org/content/vindr-cxr/
- Area: chest
- Modality: DX; CR
- Normals included: yes
- Format: DICOM
- Size: 18,000 PA radiographs (15,000 train, 3,000 test)
- License: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
- Commercial use allowed: no
- Access: credentialed
- How to access: Create a PhysioNet account, complete CITI “Data or Specimens Only Research” training, and sign the Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. Then download version 1.0.0 from the Files section.
- Limitations: Credentialed research use. You may not share the files or re-identify anyone. Labels are boxes and global findings from 17 radiologists, not full narrative reports. Training labels are three independent readers; the test set is a five-reader consensus.
- Citation: Yes. Cite the PhysioNet record and the VinDr-CXR paper named on that page. PhysioNet also asks you to contribute code with publications that use the data.
- Status: VERIFIED
- Added: 2026-10-18
- Last checked: 2026-10-18
- Page: https://hounsfieldlab.com/datasets/vindr-cxr.html
